title: Max Speed Outlier Runs
dataSources: Slopes ski sessions (`slopes:session`), Ski Tracks runs (`skitracks:run`), OnTheSnow resort reports (`onthesnow:report`), snow safety checks (`snow:safety`), and Ikon Pass lift scans (`ikon:pass`).
app: Slopes ski sessions, Ski Tracks GPS runs, OnTheSnow resort reports, snow safety checklist logs, and Ikon Pass scan exports forwarded to Splunk HEC.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=skitracks:run max_speed_kph=* trail_name=*
| eventstats avg(max_speed_kph) as avg_speed, stdev(max_speed_kph) as speed_stdev by trail_name
| eval z_score=round((max_speed_kph-avg_speed)/nullif(speed_stdev,0),2)
| where z_score>=2
| table _time trail_name max_speed_kph avg_speed z_score
description: Detects Ski Tracks runs whose max speed is two standard deviations above the trail average.
value: Speed outliers can flag icy conditions, GPS glitches, or runs where control got away from you.
implementation: Export Ski Tracks runs with `max_speed_kph` and review z-score outliers after each resort day.
visualization: Scatter plot of max speed by trail with outlier markers.
detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites

• **Splunk**: Splunk Enterprise ≥9.0 or Splunk Cloud — a single-instance home lab is fine. Create `index=personal` with 90–365 day retention (`indexes.conf`).
• **HEC token**: Settings → Data Inputs → HTTP Event Collector → New Token → index `personal`. Store the token in your connector's environment (never commit it to git).
• **Upstream product**: Personal HEC index — HTTP Event Collector token on index=personal.
• **Subcategory context**: Snow Sports & Winter Recreation — typical feeds: Slopes ski sessions (`slopes:session`), Ski Tracks runs (`skitracks:run`), OnTheSnow resort reports (`onthesnow:report`), snow safety checks (`snow:safety`), and Ikon Pass lift scans (`ikon:pass`)..
• **Sourcetypes in this search**: `skitracks:run`.
• **Network**: The connector host must reach both the vendor API/MQTT broker and your Splunk HEC port (8088/tcp).

## Step 1 — Configure data collection

Route **Personal HEC index** events into `index=personal` with `sourcetype=skitracks:run`.

**Collection method:** HTTP Event Collector token on index=personal.

**Reference endpoint / path:** `POST https://<splunk>:8088/services/collector/event`.

**Suggested poll interval:** depends on upstream connector.

**Key fields to extract:** `sourcetype-specific — see search filters`.

**Typical connector stack:** Slopes ski sessions, Ski Tracks GPS runs, OnTheSnow resort reports, snow safety checklist logs, and Ikon Pass scan exports forwarded to Splunk HEC..

**Author notes:** Export Ski Tracks runs with `max_speed_kph` and review z-score outliers after each resort day.


Example HEC payload shape:

```json
{"index": "personal", "sourcetype": "skitracks:run", "event": { ... vendor fields ... }}
```

Verify ingestion with:

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=skitracks:run earliest=-24h | head 20
```

## Step 2 — Create the search and alert

This search implements **Max Speed Outlier Runs** over `personal` data (primarily `sourcetype=skitracks:run`) across the full search range. `eventstats` / `streamstats` compute rolling baselines before filtering outliers; window size controls sensitivity (smaller window = noisier alerts).

**Fields this search depends on:** `trail_name`, `z_score`. Confirm each is populated before scheduling alerts.

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=skitracks:run max_speed_kph=* trail_name=*
| eventstats avg(max_speed_kph) as avg_speed, stdev(max_speed_kph) as speed_stdev by trail_name
| eval z_score=round((max_speed_kph-avg_speed)/nullif(speed_stdev,0),2)
| where z_score>=2
| table _time trail_name max_speed_kph avg_speed z_score
```

## Step 3 — Validate

**(a) Compare to vendor UI:** Splunk Search → index=personal | stats count by sourcetype. Totals for the same day/week should match within connector lag (usually one poll interval).

**(b) Field presence:**

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=skitracks:run earliest=-7d
| head 50
| table trail_name, z_score
```

Every column the detection uses should be non-null on recent rows.

**(c) Volume sanity:**

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=skitracks:run earliest=-30d
| timechart span=1d count
```

Flatlines usually mean a broken token, expired OAuth refresh, or HEC URL change.

**(d) Threshold calibration:** Profile `z_score` before alerting:

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=skitracks:run earliest=-30d
| stats perc50(z_score) AS p50 perc90(z_score) AS p90 perc99(z_score) AS p99 max(z_score) AS hi
```

## Step 4 — Operationalize

Create a companion dashboard titled `UC-25.91.4: Personal evidence` with the following panel layout:

**Panel 1 — Scatter Plot Of Max Speed By Trail With Outlier Markers (the key fields):** Configure according to standard Splunk visualization patterns for this panel type.


Time picker defaults: set to last 30 days with named presets for 24h, 7d, 30d, 90d, and 1y — the auditor needs all five windows without retyping. Enable scheduled PDF export for the full dashboard on the regulation's reporting cadence.

## Step 5 — Troubleshooting

**Personal HEC index — no Personal HEC index events / missing fields:** If `skitracks:run` stops updating, re-check HEC token, index `personal`, and firewall to port 8088. Search `index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd group=http_event_collector` for rejection reasons. Confirm the Personal HEC index connector script is still running (`systemctl status` or cron log).

**Personal HEC index — NULL values in extracted fields:** The Personal HEC index JSON export shape drifted — compare a raw event (`index=personal sourcetype=skitracks:run | head 1 | spath`) against the field names in Step 2. Re-map in the connector before changing the SPL.

**Personal HEC index — API error / auth denied (401/403):** Refresh tokens expire on most consumer APIs — re-authorize the scripted input, update `passwords.conf` / env vars, and verify the vendor developer app is not in sandbox mode.

**Personal HEC index — endpoint timeout / HTTP 429 throttling:** Back off the poll interval in the connector; Personal HEC index APIs often cap requests per 15 minutes on free tiers.

**Everything is an outlier:** Baseline window is too short or `stdev=0` — require minimum sample count (`where count>=5`) before computing z-scores.

**Stale dashboard:** Confirm the saved search `dispatch.earliest_time` covers enough history for your `aggregation` buckets.
